transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Democrats and Republicans are spending heavily in dozens of House races between now and election day next week.
An NPR analysis finds 70 districts where both parties are investing six-figure sums in advertising.
NPR's Stephen Fowler has details.
Spending data from Ad Impact suggests the question is less about whether there will be a Democratic wave in the House,
but rather how high it could crest.
Several races will see more than $10 million in ads between now and Tuesday,
including toss-up races in Michigan, North Carolina, New York, and Florida.
Seven-figure ad buys in very conservative communities in Tennessee, Oklahoma, and Arkansas,
and last-minute resources to districts where gerrymandering by Republicans could backfire.
These 70 districts voted for Trump by an average of nine points in 2024,
highlighting the impact of the Trump administration's unpopularity with voters over the last year.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News, Atlanta.
More than 90 percent of the votes are counted in Israel's elections,
and there's still no clear majority that determines whether Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stays
or steps aside for his main rival, Gadi Isincote.
And Piers Daniel Estrin says one faction could break the impasse in the election,
the first held since the Hamas-led attack and subsequent start of the war in Gaza three years ago.
Isincote's camp could win if they would be willing to partner with Arab-led parties,
which have gained about 19 seats in parliament.
That is a record for parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel.
But that does not appear to be likely.
It's too risky politically for Isincote.
There has been a lot of demonization of Arab political leaders in Israel.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reporting.
Hackers crack the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's personnel files,
exposing names, phone numbers and addresses of more than 40,000 DHS employees.
Here's NPR's Vanessa Romo.
An activist group called the Department of Peace stole troves of data
by subverting DHS's single sign-on system, according to an online statement.
Now that information, which identifies 21,000 employees with the U.S. Customs and Border Protection,
and reveals about 7,000 ICE employees, is available in a searchable database.
Ryan Adegnon, one of the activists who helped create it, says publishing the data is a public service.
Employees of the DHS need to be able to be identified
and have their names out there for reasons like sending public records requests.
In a message attached to the database, the hacker said, quote,
"They have our information, so it's only fair that we have theirs."
Vanessa Romo, NPR News.
According to at least three U.S. officials not authorized to speak publicly,
Defense Secretary Pete Hexeth has ousted another top general from the Pentagon.
Officials tell NPR Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia is a subject of a leak investigation.
It's NPR.
A court hearing is scheduled today on whether New York Attorney General Letitia James
should be disqualified from leading the criminal investigation into an alleged gang rape at Cornell in 2024.
Attorneys for two of the men named in the accuser's lawsuit cite the social media post
in which they say James has displayed bias against them before the probe has even begun.
James' office says that the challenge has no merit.
In the final set of major economic data before Tuesday's midterms,
the Commerce Department reveals inflation remained elevated.
However, economic growth also picked up last quarter.
Brewers fans are riding high.
Milwaukee clinched its first World Series title after beating the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5 last night, 4-1.
Steve Futterman reports from St. Petersburg, Florida.
Game 5 was controlled by Milwaukee almost from start to finish.
The Brewers jumped out to a 1-0 lead in the second inning,
made it 2-0 in the fifth, 4-0 in the sixth before Tampa Bay scored its only run in the ninth.
One of the breakout stars for Milwaukee during the series was 22-year-old rookie Cooper Pratt.
He had eight hits and drove in seven runs.
This is unbelievable.
It was just one of the first World Series in Brewers history.
I was only here for four months, but a lot of these guys have been here for a long time.
The Brewers franchise began play in 1969.
This is the first time it has won the championship.
Tampa Bay is still looking for its first title.
That's Steve Futterman.
It's NPR.
